standard.title: Effects of Population Movements and Settlement Changes in the Industrial Period
standard.description: the short-, medium- and long-term effects of population movements and changing settlement patterns during this period, such as global demographic changes, transport, new ideas, and political and social reforms
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have studied the causes and effects of the Industrial Revolution (AC9HH9K13) and the specific population movements of the period (AC9HH9K014). They understand the technological and economic drivers of change. This descriptor asks them to examine the temporal span of the effects — short, medium, and long-term — across demographic, transport, ideational, and reform dimensions.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students describe the short-, medium- and long-term effects of population movements and changing settlement patterns during the industrial period.

nodes.label: Environmental and demographic impacts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can describe the impact of factories, mines and cities on the environment and on population growth and distribution.
nodes.minimum_width: Describe one environmental and one demographic impact of the Industrial Revolution on population and settlement.
nodes.typical_width: Describe the impact of factories, mines and cities on the environment (river pollution, air quality, industrial waste, urban overcrowding); describe how industrialisation transformed population distribution (rural-to-urban shift, growth of industrial cities, population growth from improved food supply and medicine); explain how these changes were interconnected.
wider: Investigate the public health crisis in industrial cities (e.g. cholera outbreaks in London or Manchester) as a consequence of rapid urbanisation without infrastructure — examining how demographic change outpaced the capacity of cities to support their populations
Examine the long-term demographic legacy of industrial-era population movement — tracking urbanisation rates from 1800 to 1900 using historical data — to assess the scale of the transformation

response_modes.reason: Covering both environmental (pollution, degradation) and demographic (growth, distribution) impacts prevents students from treating only one dimension and gives a fuller picture of how settlement change operated.

success_criteria: Describes at least two environmental impacts of industrialisation on the natural environment
Describes how industrialisation changed population distribution, with at least one specific example

nodes.label: Steam engine's impact on transport and industry
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can investigate the impact of the development of the steam engine on transport, manufacturing and trade, and explain how transport change enabled further population movement.
nodes.minimum_width: Explain how the steam engine changed either transport or manufacturing, with one specific example.
nodes.typical_width: Investigate the impact of the steam engine on transport (railways, steam ships), manufacturing (powered mills, larger factories), and trade (faster distribution of goods, expanded markets); explain how transport transformation enabled larger-scale population movements and connected previously isolated communities to industrial centres.
wider: Examine how the expansion of the British railway network from 1830–1870 physically reshaped both the economy and the geography of settlement — analysing which regions grew, which declined, and why
Investigate the steam ship's role in enabling mass migration — examining how lower fares and faster journeys transformed transatlantic migration from a rare event to a mass phenomenon

response_modes.reason: Connecting transport change to both manufacturing efficiency and population movement shows how the steam engine had cascading effects — not just as a machine but as an enabler of the entire industrial-era demographic transformation.

success_criteria: Explains at least two ways the steam engine changed transport or manufacturing
Explains how at least one transport change enabled population movement at greater scale

nodes.label: Social, political and reform effects
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain how social and political reforms resulting from industrialisation led to higher standards of living for many people, including in health care, education, and workplace rights.
nodes.minimum_width: Describe at least two social or political reforms that resulted from industrialisation and explain their effects on living standards.
nodes.typical_width: Explain how social and political reforms resulted in higher standards of living including: public health reform (clean water, sewage systems), educational reform (compulsory schooling), workplace reforms (Factory Acts, limits on child labour), and political reforms (extension of voting rights, trade union rights); explain how these reforms were short-, medium-, and long-term responses to the problems of industrialisation.
wider: Examine the Factory Acts as evidence of how political pressure from workers and reformers changed the legal relationship between employers and employees — tracing how specific legislation responded to specific documented abuses

Investigate the connection between urbanisation and the extension of voting rights — examining how the growing urban working class created political pressure for democratic reform (e.g. the Reform Act 1832 in Britain)

Examine how public health reform (clean water supply, sewage systems) saved more lives than medical treatment in the 19th century — using mortality data to assess the health impact of infrastructure investment

response_modes.reason: This node integrates the problems of industrialisation (Nodes 1–2) with the reform responses — demonstrating how social and political change was driven by the problems industrialisation created. The short/medium/long-term framework organises the temporal dimension.

success_criteria: Describes at least two social or political reforms produced by industrialisation
Explains how reforms improved living standards, with reference to specific historical changes
